t.E363.agn: The SCF in 1991 and JECFA in 1986 decided that no numerical ADI was needed for succinic acid ('not specified'). EFSA issued a new call for data in 2024 for the re-evaluation in the EU; it stated that no data had been received in response to the earlier calls in 2010 and 2012.
t.E363.body: Succinic acid is a normal intermediate of the citric acid cycle (energy production) in the body and occurs naturally in plants and animals.
t.E363.found.2: Powdered drink mixes for home preparation
t.E363.prod: May be produced chemically by hydrogenation of maleic acid or fumaric acid, or by fermentation.
t.E363.regx.0: Re-evaluation ongoing; a call for data was issued in 2024. The SCF had set the ADI as 'not specified' in 1991.
t.E363.regx.2: Permitted only in certain categories (e.g. 6000 mg/kg in desserts and flavoured fermented milk products, 5000 mg/kg in soups, 3000 mg/kg in powdered drinks).
t.E363.summary: An organic acid that also occurs in nature. It gives a sour taste; used as an acidity regulator in soups and desserts.
t.E363.what: An organic acid that gives sourness and regulates acidity.
